name: MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.CAR.tracialRepresentation
title: The GNS representation of the target trace extension

content.display_title: The GNS representation of the target trace extension
content.one_sentence_role: The chosen state on the existing target supplies its cyclic GNS representation.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be the completed CAR algebra and $\tau$ its normalized trace. Fix a representative shell family and its chosen unitary links $L_j$ in the selected atomic representation $\pi$. Write $T=C^*(\pi(A),\{L_j\})$ for the resulting concrete target and $\iota:A\to T$, $\iota(a)=\pi(a)$, for its faithful unital source map. This fixes one target and one source map throughout. Let $\phi$ be the chosen state extension of $\tau$ to $T$. Define $\rho_\phi:T\to B(H_\phi)$ to be its GNS representation.
content.definition_explanation:
Choose $\phi$ from `exists_state_extension_trace` and regard that same functional as a positive linear map. Form the GNS completion of $T$ modulo its null vectors, set $H_\phi$ to that Hilbert space, and let $\xi_\phi=[1]$. The induced left action is

$$\rho_\phi(t)[b]=[tb],\qquad \phi(t)=\langle\xi_\phi,\rho_\phi(t)\xi_\phi\rangle.$$

The right-hand side of the definition is exactly the GNS star homomorphism of `traceExtensionPositive family`. This positive-map bundle has the same values as $\phi$; it is not another state. Normalization gives $\|\xi_\phi\|=1$, so $\xi_\phi\ne0$ and $H_\phi$ is nonzero. The GNS construction gives the dense $T$-orbit. Its restriction realizes $\tau$ because $\phi\circ\iota=\tau$. The actual-representation source-cyclicity theorem applies to these two facts and proves the source orbit dense; it is not an assumption smuggled into the definition.
content.assumptions: A representative shell family is fixed first. The chosen extension is positive and normalized; its traciality is not needed to perform the GNS construction.
content.conclusion:
With its canonical unit vector $\xi_\phi$, this representation realizes $\phi$ and has dense target orbit. The separately proved source-cyclicity result also gives

$$\overline{\{\rho_\phi(\iota(a))\xi_\phi:a\in A\}}=H_\phi.$$

Consequently $H_\phi$ is separable, since $A$ is separable and the displayed orbit map is continuous.
content.lean_realization_notes: Separability here is a conclusion about the Hilbert space. The algebra $T$ is not assumed norm separable. Injectivity of $\rho_\phi$ is a separate theorem; irreducibility or purity of $\phi$ is not asserted.
